title: Adaptive cross-GPU KV compaction and live rebalance for pipeline-aware continuous batching
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Reduce tail latency and OOMs for mixed pipeline/tensor parallel model serving under continuous batching by dynamically compacting underutilized KV entries and rebalancing KV ownership across GPUs while preserving pipeline stage locality and minimizing cache thrash.

Context: Continuous batching keeps workers busy with variable sequence lengths and prefix reuse. Current static shard maps allocate KV slices at model load and rarely adapt to run-time hotkey distributions, leading to fragmentation, imbalanced memory pressure, and spill events. Tensor and pipeline parallelism interact: some pipeline stages accumulate hot prefixes, others remain underutilized, and naive cross-GPU migration breaks pipeline locality and increases inter-stage synchronization costs.

Approach summary: Implement a three-part system: (1) intra-GPU compaction engine that coalesces short-lived KV slabs and reorganizes slab free lists with minimal locking; (2) cross-GPU rebalance controller that observes per-GPU live-set heatmaps and issues low-impact ownership transfers for cold micro-slices; (3) pipeline-aware migration policy that pins hot prefixes to GPUs co-located with their compute stage and schedules migrations during predicted low-latency windows (between pipeline micro-batches).

Key algorithms and heuristics:
- Compact-on-threshold: trigger compaction when free-fragmentation > 20% for a slab class and live-alloc rate slows for > 500ms.
- Micro-slice candidates: define smallest migratable unit as contiguous KV micro-slice (~64KB aligned) containing full attention key/value pairs to avoid split-key reads.
- Heat decay windows: maintain an exponential decay heat score per micro-slice (alpha=0.1, tick=100ms) to detect stable cold slices versus transient dips.
- Migration budget: limit cross-GPU bandwidth to 10% of the interconnect to prevent interference; apply backoff when observed tail latency rises > 10%.
- Pipeline affinity score: combine compute-stage locality, upcoming prefix reuse predictions (from prefix-cache telemetry), and estimated migration cost to decide whether to migrate a candidate.

Integration with runtime:
- New lightweight signals exported from executor: per-stage KV hit/miss, live-alloc rate, per-slice heat score.
- Rebalance controller runs in control-plane thread and coordinates with job-level scheduler to pick safe transfer windows.
- Prefetch hooks: when a migration is planned, downstream stages register a temporary prefetch to hide transfer latency for hot prefixes.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Consistency: we avoid split-write ownership by using ownership handoff protocol (source marks slice in-transit; destination spikes temporary readonly replica; final switch under epoch boundary). This increases memory temporarily.
- Cost vs. benefit: migration is beneficial only for sustained imbalance; short-lived spikes are handled by intra-GPU compaction and admission control.
- Hardware heterogeneity: controller uses per-GPU memory headroom and NVLink/PCIe bandwidth profiles to make placement decisions.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Reduce KV-related OOM incidents by >= 75% on mixed workloads.
- 95th percentile gen latency reduction of >= 15% for deployments exhibiting cross-stage hotkey skew.
- Migration bandwidth overhead < 8% of interconnect on steady-state.

Compatibility and rollout: feature gated by runtime flag 'adaptive_kv_rebalance'. Start with canary on dedicated clusters, enable pilot for a subset of customer workloads. Default migration budget conservative; telemetry will be collected to tune thresholds.

Deliverables: design doc, control-plane implementation, compaction engine, migration protocol, integration tests, benchmarks, rollout playbook.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Initial ticket created after load-test incident where a small fraction of pipeline stages caused repeated OOMs during long-prefix chat workloads. Linked design doc and initial heatmap data.
2026-03-11 — Design review with Runtime and Serving teams. Agreed to prefer micro-slice migration unit to avoid split-key penalties. Miguel requested clearer invariants for handoff protocol.
2026-03-12 — Spike completed: intra-GPU compaction prototype reduced fragmentation on test harness by 42% with negligible CPU overhead (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2483).
2026-03-13 — UX/Console: add telemetry panels for per-GPU heatmaps and migration events (PM: Lina Chen). Linking draft dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kv-rebalance-canary
2026-03-14 — Security reviewed high-level protocol; requested explicit KMS audit for migrations in Private deployments. Added security_review_required flag.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end feature merged behind feature flag and covered by unit/integration tests
Benchmarks show >= 15% P95 latency reduction on targeted skewed workloads
Migration protocol implements in-transit marker and epoch switch without data races
Telemetry exposes per-slice heat scores and migration counters in Console
Runbook for canary rollback and OOM mitigation documented
notes: Decision: do not perform eager eviction of hot prefixes during migration windows; prefer transient replication and lazy switch to preserve tail latency.
Follow-up: evaluate machine-learning driven prefix reuse predictor in Q3 to improve migration accuracy.
Edge-case: for single-GPU deployments, compaction engine still runs but rebalance controller is no-op.
